shock.adult_dose: Balanced Salt Solution (e.g., Ringer's Lactate): 500ml IV bolus
shock.notes_updates: Balanced Salt Solutions preferred over 0.9% Saline for septic shock to prevent hyperchloraemic acidosis.
0.9% Saline remains primary for hypovolaemia due to blood loss/dehydration.

inotropes.notes_updates: First-line vasopressor for septic shock. No longer restricted as 'Section 21'.
Second-line for septic shock if MAP targets not met with Noradrenaline.
Indicated for septic shock with cardiac dysfunction (persistent hypoperfusion despite fluids/vasopressors).
Largely superseded by Noradrenaline for shock. Standard starting dose is 5 ug/kg/min.

resuscitation_medication.paediatric_dose: 10ug/kg IV OR 0.1ml/kg of 1:10 000 (1mg adrenaline/10ml normal saline)

resuscitation_medication.adult_dose: 300mg IV bolus over 3min (unstable pt); 150mg IV bolus over 3min (stable pt)

sedation.notes: Preferred for asthma/bronchospasm or trauma intubation

sedation.notes_updates: Avoid routine deep sedation; prioritize pain control and neuro-psychological support.
Adjust dose in obesity. Caution: Propofol Infusion Syndrome (PRIS).
Preferred for asthma/bronchospasm or trauma intubation.

seizures.adult_dose: 10mg IM or buccal (if no IV access)

seizures.notes_updates: Antipsychotic for severe agitation or delirium

analgesia.notes_updates: Good for renal failure or unstable BP

neuroprotective.notes_updates: Monitor osmolar gap; avoid if hypotensive
Alternative to mannitol for raised ICP

broad_spectrum_antibiotics.notes_updates: Extended infusion: 3-4hr. High dose for meningitis

hyperkalaemia_management.notes: Drives K+ into cells. Monitor glucose q15min

diuretics.notes: Monitor electrolytes. Ototoxicity at high doses

vitamins.notes: Give BEFORE glucose in malnourished/alcoholic patients

protocols.adult_dose: NAC Old Regimen: 150mg/kg in 200ml 5% Dextrose IV over 1hr, then 50mg/kg in 500ml 5% Dextrose IV over 4hrs, then 100mg/kg in 1L 5% Dextrose IV over 16hrs | NAC SNAP Protocol: 100mg/kg in 200ml 5% Dextrose IV over 2hrs, then 200mg/kg in 1L 5% Dextrose IV over 10hrs
protocols.notes: Toxic dose: 150mg/kg or >10g in adults. Use nomogram to establish need for antidote. Start <8hrs if possible. If in doubt, give NAC.

protocols.adult_dose: Naloxone 0.4-4mg IV q2-3min up to 10mg total | Infusion: 0.04-0.16mg/kg/hr IV
protocols.notes: Reversal agent has shorter half-life than most opioids (~1 hour). Monitor for recurrent sedation.

protocols.adult_dose: Flumazenil: 0.2mg IV over 15sec, then 0.1mg every 60sec (max 1mg) | Caution: Generally AVOID Flumazenil
protocols.notes: AVOID Flumazenil - can precipitate withdrawal/seizures in chronic users or co-ingestions. Supportive care is primary.

protocols.adult_dose: Atropine: 0.04-0.05mg/kg IV (3-5mg adult), double every 5min until atropinised | Infusion: 200mg Atropine in 200ml 0.9% NaCl (1mg/ml), 10-20% of total dose/hr
protocols.notes: Decontamination is key. Endpoint is clearing of pulmonary secretions, NOT tachycardia or pupil size.

reversal_agents.adult_dose: 4-Factor PCC: 25-50 IU/kg IV; Vitamin K: 5-10mg IV slowly (life-threatening bleed)
reversal_agents.notes_updates: Do NOT wait for INR result in catastrophic bleeding. PCC (Haemosolvex) is 4-factor.

formulae.standard_dilutions: Standard: 12 mg (12 amps) in 200 mL N/S (60 mcg/mL)

formulae.formula: Dose x weight x 60 / prepared concentration
Na deficit = 0.6 x Wt(kg) x (Desired Na - Actual Na)
Page 92: Na + [1.6 x (Glucose - 5.5) / 5.5] for glucose 11-22; use 2.4 if glucose >22

antihypertensives.notes_updates: Mixed alpha/beta blocker. Good for hypertensive emergencies

heart_failure.notes_updates: Check levels. Toxicity: nausea, visual changes, arrhythmias

anticoagulation.notes_updates: Anti-Xa monitoring in renal impairment, pregnancy

steroids.notes_updates: Stress dose for adrenal insufficiency, septic shock

endocrine.notes_updates: Check glucose hourly. Hold if K+ <3.3

symptoms: Chest pain, pressure, tightness, or squeezing (may radiate to neck, jaw, back, or left arm)
Atypical symptoms: dyspnoea, epigastric pain, unexplained fatigue, or syncope (common in elderly, females, diabetics)
Anginal equivalent: acute shortness of breath without clear cause
signs: New mitral regurgitation murmur (papillary muscle dysfunction/rupture)
Bilateral lung crackles (acute heart failure/pulmonary edema)

management_steps.details: Triage as ORANGE. Perform 12-lead & 15-lead ECG (including V4R for RV infarct, and V7-9 for true posterior MI) within 10 minutes.
Give Aspirin 300 mg chewed stat, unless known hypersensitivity (if allergic, give Clopidogrel 300 mg PO stat).
If SBP >= 90 and HR 50-100: Nitroglycerin SL spray (1 spray q5min, max 3) or sublingual tablets. If pain is unrelieved by nitrates: Fentanyl 50 mcg IV aliquots.

STEMI/OMI door-to-needle time is 30 mins! LMWH (Clexane) 30mg IV stat then 1mg/kg SC (or UFH 60 IU/kg IV), Clopidogrel 300mg PO, Simvastatin 40mg PO, and Atenolol 50mg PO (if no bradycardia, HF, or asthma).

warnings: RV Infarction (V4R STE): Avoid Nitroglycerin and Beta-blockers. Treat hypotension with IV fluid boluses (20ml/kg) to maintain preload.
Nitroglycerin Contraindications: SBP < 90, HR < 50 or > 100, RV infarction, or PDE5 inhibitor use within 24-48h.

management_steps.details: These indicate critical coronary occlusion without classic STE: (1) De Winter syndrome (V1-6 J-point depression with tall symmetric T waves), (2) Posterior STEMI (horizontal STD in V1-3, tall R in V1-2), (3) Wellens Sign A (biphasic T waves in V2-3) or Sign B (deeply inverted anterior T waves), (4) Shark fin pattern, (5) Hyperacute T waves.

Score >= 3 has 90% specificity for MI: (1) Criteria A (5 pts): concordant STE >= 1mm in any lead, (2) Criteria B (3 pts): concordant STD >= 1mm in V1, V2, or V3, (3) Criteria C (2 pts): discordant STE >= 5mm in any lead (Modified: STE >= 25% of preceding S-wave).

warnings: Failure to recognize STEMI equivalents leads to catastrophic treatment delays. Actively look for them in chest pain patients with normal or non-diagnostic ECGs.

management_steps.details: Check glucose immediately (rule out hypoglycaemia). Assess GCS and clinical onset time. Exclude other mimics: Todd's paresis, migraine, tumour, encephalitis.
Verify absence of intracranial hemorrhage. Consult neurology/stroke team immediately.
If within 3-4.5h and no contraindications: Alteplase 0.9 mg/kg IV (10% bolus over 1 min, remainder over 60 mins). Max dose 90mg. Keep SBP < 185 and DBP < 110.
If bleeding is suspected: stop Alteplase, order urgent CT brain, send clotting studies, transfuse Cryoprecipitate 10 U/kg IV over 10-30 min, and give Tranexamic Acid 1g IV.

warnings: Absolute Contraindications: Prior ICH, known vascular lesion (AVM), malignant neoplasm, active bleeding, stroke/trauma within 3 months, SBP > 185 / DBP > 110 despite treatment, INR > 1.7.

symptoms: Severe dyspnoea, orthopnoea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea (PND), effort intolerance.
signs: Tachycardia, tachypnoea, elevated JVP, bilateral lung crackles, third heart sound (gallop rhythm), hepatomegaly, peripheral pitting edema.

management_steps.details: Sit patient upright (>45 degrees). Apply high-flow oxygen. Triage to RESUS if in acute distress.
Initiate CPAP or BiPAP early (PEEP of 4-10 cmH2O) to decrease work of breathing and improve preload/afterload.
If SBP > 90: Nitrocine (vasodilator) 1-2 mg IV bolus or infusion 30 ug/min (titrate up to 150-200 ug/min). Furosemide (Lasix) 20-40 mg IV (or patient's daily PO dose as IV bolus).
If SBP < 90 with signs of hypoperfusion: start Dobutamine infusion 2.5-10 ug/kg/min (avoid in pure diastolic dysfunction or severe aortic stenosis).

Unstable AF (causing chest pain, hypotension, acute heart failure, dyspnoea, or altered GCS): Perform urgent synchronized cardioversion (150-200 J) under sedation. Give Clexane 1 mg/kg SC stat unless contraindicated.
If < 48 hours and no structural heart disease: consider rhythm control (electrical or chemical with Amiodarone 150mg over 30 mins). If > 48 hours: prioritize rate control (goal < 110 bpm).
Beta-blocker (Atenolol 50mg PO or Carvedilol 3.125mg PO) OR Calcium Channel Blocker (Diltiazem/Verapamil) OR Digoxin (if heart failure present). Alternatively, Amiodarone infusion.
Calculate CHA2DS2-VASc and HAS-BLED scores to guide long-term anticoagulation. Start SC Clexane 1mg/kg 12h if thromboembolism risk is high.

warnings: WPW + Atrial Fibrillation (Wide QRS, rate > 200, irregular): DO NOT give nodal blocking agents (Beta-blockers, CCBs, Digoxin, Amiodarone) as it will precipitate VF! Perform immediate synchronized electrical cardioversion.

management_steps.details: Mild: Pulse < 100, Sats > 95, PEFR > 75%. Moderate: Pulse 100-120, Sats 90-95, PEFR 50-70%. Severe: Pulse > 120, Sats < 90, PEFR < 50%, or silent chest.
All patients: Salbutamol/Fenoterol + Ipratropium Bromide (Atrovent) nebulisations continuously or every 20 minutes.
Give Hydrocortisone 200mg IV stat (or oral Prednisone 0.5mg/kg). If severe/refractory: give Magnesium Sulphate 2g (25-50mg/kg in children) IV over 20 minutes.

Avoid intubation if possible! If required, perform RSI with Ketamine 1mg/kg. Set ventilator to Volume Assist Control, TV 6ml/kg, RR 10-12, I:E ratio 1:3 to 1:5 to allow long expiration. Pre-load with fluids.
Titrate oxygen carefully to target Sats 88-92% (prevent hypercapnic respiratory drive failure). Deliver Salbutamol + Ipratropium Bromide nebs.
Give Hydrocortisone 200mg IV stat (or Prednisone 0.5mg/kg PO). If infection is suspected (increased sputum volume/purulence/fever): Augmentin 1g BD PO (or 1.2g IV) + Azithromycin 500mg PO daily.
NIV (BiPAP) is highly effective for COPD respiratory acidosis (pH < 7.35, PaCO2 > 45mmHg). Reduces intubation rates dramatically.
ABCD survey. Establish large-bore IVs. Administer 30ml/kg balanced crystalloid bolus (Ringer's Lactate/Balsol) for hypotension or Lactate > 4.
Measure Lactate. Obtain blood cultures PRIOR to antibiotics (aerobic bottle ONLY, minimum 10ml, preferably 20ml). Administer broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 hour.
If persistent hypotension despite fluids: start Adrenaline/Noradrenaline infusion to maintain MAP >= 65 mmHg. Re-measure lactate if initial lactate was high.

warnings: Blood cultures must always be taken BEFORE the first dose of antibiotics.
Be extremely cautious with aggressive fluids in patients with cardiac dysfunction or elderly (risk of acute pulmonary edema).

management_steps.details: ABCD. Keep NPO. Insert 2x large-bore IVs. Administer warm Balsol/Ringer's Lactate (10ml/kg).

Transfuse PRCs if haemodynamically unstable despite crystalloid bolus, Hb < 7 in low-risk, or Hb < 9 in high-risk/elderly/coronary disease. If coagulopathic (INR > 1.5) or on Warfarin: give FFP 10-20ml/kg or PCC.

Give Pantoprazole (Pantoloc) 80mg IV loading dose, then start infusion (200mg in 200ml N/S at 8 ml/hr). If variceal/cirrhosis: give Ceftriaxone 1g IV + Octreotide 50mcg bolus followed by 50mcg/hr infusion.
Notify surgical/gastroenterology registrar on call urgently. Consider Sengstaken-Blakemore tube if catastrophic variceal bleeding.

warnings: Avoid over-transfusion in suspected variceal bleeds (increases portal pressure and worsens haemorrhage).
There is NO role for Tranexamic Acid (TXA) in upper GI bleeding.

management_steps.details: If unstable/shocked: Triage to RESUS. Insert 2x large-bore IVs. Send bloods for FBC, U&E, Crossmatch, and VBG. Transfuse emergency group O negative blood.
Check urine pregnancy test and perform bedside ultrasound: look for viable IUP, non-viable/incomplete products, empty uterus with free fluid (ruptured ectopic).

Ectopic: Urgent gynae consult, prepare for surgery. Incomplete Miscarriage: Rub up uterus, expel products, start Oxytocin infusion (20 units in 1L fluid at 125ml/hr). Septic Miscarriage: Augmentin 30mg/kg IV.
Rub up uterus, expel products, start Oxytocin infusion, give Tranexamic Acid 1g IV over 10 min, insert Foley catheter to empty bladder, and consider balloon tamponade.

warnings: Do NOT perform digital PV examination in antepartum haemorrhage (>24 weeks) if placenta praevia is suspected — confirm on ultrasound first.
Rh-negative mothers with vaginal bleeding require anti-D immunoglobulin (within 72 hours).

management_steps.details: Sudden onset severe back/flank/abdominal pain with syncope/shock. On palpation: pulsatile mass. On POCUS: aorta > 3cm (aneurysmal), > 6cm (high risk rupture). Unstable patients need immediate THEATRE, NOT CT! Aim for permissive hypotension (SBP 80-90 mmHg), give TXA 1g IV, and notify vascular surgery.

Sudden tearing central chest pain radiating to back. Signs: BP/pulse discrepancy in arms, new aortic regurgitation murmur. Urgent CTA. Control BP & HR: start Labetalol infusion (target pulse < 60, SBP < 110). If BP still high, add Nitroglycerin infusion.

The 6 P's: Pain, Pallor, Pulselessness, Paresthesia, Paralysis, Poikilothermia (cold limb). Embolus vs Thrombosis. Perform handheld Doppler, check ABI (< 0.5 is severe). Give IV Heparin bolus (80 U/kg) and refer to vascular surgery urgently.
Triage as ORANGE. Check FBC, malaria smear & antigen. Look for high-risk criteria: children, pregnant, elderly, splenectomy.

If smear/antigen positive with < 5% parasitaemia and no organ dysfunction: give Co-artem 4 tablets PO stat, 4 after 8 hours, then BD for 2 days. If unavailable: Quinine + Doxycycline (or Quinine + Clindamycin in pregnancy/children).

Smear > 5%, or any organ dysfunction (coma, convulsions, pulmonary edema, shock, jaundice, severe anaemia Hb < 5, hypoglycemia < 2.2, lactate > 5): Give Artesunate 2.4 mg/kg IV stat at 0, 12, 24 hours. (Alternative: Quinine infusion).

warnings: Observe for vomiting for 1 hour in the ED after oral antimalarial. If vomiting occurs within 1 hour, re-administer the dose. If vomiting persists, refer to Internal Medicine.

management_steps.details: Onset: sudden/thunderclap (SAH), post-traumatic. Symptoms: altered GCS, seizure, focal neurology, meningism (meningitis), fever. Comorbidities: malignancy, pregnancy (pre-eclampsia), HIV. Medications: anticoagulants.

Tension: bilateral pressure/tightness, mild-mod. Migraine: gradual unilateral pulsating, photophobia, visual auras, mod-severe. Cluster: rapid peri-orbital excruciating, ipsilateral eye redness/lacrimation, rhinorrhoea, Horner's syndrome, severe.
Tension: NSAIDs, Paracetamol. Migraine: Metoclopramide, triptans, NSAIDs, consider steroids. AVOID OPIOIDS! Cluster: 100% Oxygen high flow, paracetamol, triptans, steroids, ketamine if refractory.

Peripheral (vestibular neuritis, labyrinthitis, BPPV): Sudden onset, severe, intermittent, horizontal unilateral nystagmus. Central (posterior stroke, cerebellar hemorrhage, tumor): Gradual/sudden, mild, continuous, purely vertical or direction-changing nystagmus, neurological deficits present.

management_steps.action: Apply HINTS bedside exam (for Acute Vestibular Syndrome)
management_steps.details: Rule out central cause: (1) Head Impulse Test (peripheral = catchup saccade, central = no saccade/normal - worrying!), (2) Nystagmus (peripheral = unilateral horizontal, central = direction-changing or vertical), (3) Test of Skew (central = refixation present after uncover, peripheral = no refixation).
BPPV: Dix-Hallpike maneuver to elicit nystagmus and confirm affected canal. Epley maneuver to reposition canaliths and resolve symptoms.
Place supine, elevate legs. Stop trigger.
0.5ml neat 1:1000 IM in anterolateral thigh. Repeat q3-5min if required.
20ml/kg Crystalloid bolus (Ringer's Lactate/Balsol). Airway management ready.
Hydrocortisone 200mg IV stat + Promethazine 12.5mg slow IV.

warnings: Biphasic reaction occurs in 5-20% of cases — monitor for 4-8 hours minimum
Avoid beta-blockers as they cause unopposed alpha-agonism during treatment

management_steps.action: Assess Airway & Prepare for difficult airway
management_steps.details: Stridor, drooling, dyspnoea are red flags. Double surgical setup ready.
If ACE-I induced (Bradykinin-mediated): Adrenaline, steroids, antihistamines are ineffective. Give Tranexamic Acid 1g IV over 10 min + FFP 2 units.
Muscarinic (DUMBELS): Diaphoresis, Urination, Miosis, Bradycardia/bronchorrhoea, Emesis, Lacrimation, Salivation. Nicotinic: Fasciculations, weakness, HT, tachycardia, mydriasis. CNS: seizures, coma.
Universal precautions. Remove clothing, wash skin with soap and water. If intubation required, avoid succinylcholine (causes prolonged paralysis).
Atropine 0.04-0.05 mg/kg IV stat (3-5mg adult). Double every 5 mins until atropinised. Infusion: 200mg Atropine in 200ml saline (1mg/ml), run at 10-20% of total dose already given/hr.
Benzodiazepines only for seizures (No phenytoin). Monitor and correct electrolytes. Weakness (nicotinic symptom) may require prolonged intubation.

warnings: Thrombolytic / Antidote Endpoint: CLEARING OF RESPIRATORY SECRETIONS (Atropinisation), NOT tachycardia or pupil size.

management_steps.details: Symptoms: hypotension, bradycardia, CCB (hyperglycaemia), BB (hypoglycaemia), acidosis, GCS depression. Insert 2x large-bore IVs.
Give Calcium Chloride 10ml 10% over 10 min (target Ca 2 mmol). Consider activated charcoal 50g via NGT if within 1 hour.
Start with 50ml 50% dextrose bolus. Actrapid 1 IU/kg IV stat. Then Actrapid infusion of 0.5 IU/kg/hr, titrate every 30 mins to max 10 IU/kg/hr. Dextrose infusion 25g/hr to maintain euglycemia.
Monitor HGT every 20 mins for 1st hour, then hourly. Monitor and replace Potassium if < 2.5.
Airway, breathing, circulation. Seizure control (benzodiazepines). Correct hypoglycaemia and hyperthermia. Resuscitation antidotes.
Inquire: Agent, dose, time of ingestion, co-ingestants. Give activated charcoal 1g/kg if within 1 hour.

Atropine (organophosphates), Calcium/HIET (CCB/BB), Desferrioxamine (Iron), Ethanol (Methanol), N-acetylcysteine (Paracetamol), Pyridoxine (Isoniazid), Sodium Bicarbonate (TCA/salicylates), Vitamin K/FFP (Warfarin).
Toxic dose: 150mg/kg or > 10g in adults. Measure paracetamol level at >= 4 hours post ingestion. Check blood gas, U&E, salicylate level.
(1) 100mg/kg in 200ml 5% Dextrose IV over 2 hours, then (2) 200mg/kg in 1L 5% Dextrose IV over 10 hours.
(1) 150mg/kg in 200ml 5% D-5-W over 1 hour, (2) 50mg/kg in 500ml over 4 hours, (3) 100mg/kg in 1L over 16 hours.
INH depletes Vit B6 -> decreased GABA -> seizures and severe high anion gap metabolic acidosis (HAGMA) with lactic acidosis.

If known amount ingested: 1g Pyridoxine for each gram of INH, max 5g. If unknown: give 5g total (200 tablets of 25mg, crush and give via NGT once airway secured) or IV if available. Repeat in 10-20 min if seizures continue.
Triage to RESUS. Send INR. Administer 4-Factor PCC (Haemosolvex) 25-50 IU/kg IV. If PCC unavailable, FFP 10-15 ml/kg IV. Give Vitamin K 5-10mg IV slow infusion. Recheck INR in 30 mins.
INR 3-4.5: omit/lower next dose. INR 4.5-10: stop, give oral Vit K 1-2.5mg if high bleeding risk. INR > 10: stop, give oral Vit K 2.5-5mg. Resume at lower dose once therapeutic.

Thick tail & slender pincers = highly venomous (Parabuthus granulatus / transvaalicus). Symptoms of severe envenomation: severe local pain, generalised paresthesia, tremors, muscle cramps, agitation, drooling, cardiac arrhythmias.
Standard dose is 5-10 ml IV diluted in small volume saline given over 15 minutes. May take 2-6 hours to reach effect. Re-administer 5ml after 6 hours if inadequate response.
Infiltrate sting site with local anaesthetic. AVOID OPIOIDS (increases respiratory depression). For muscle cramps: Calcium Gluconate 10% IV (Adults 10ml, children 0.5ml/kg).

Neurotoxic (Cape Cobra, Black Mamba): weakness, ptosis, paralysis, respiratory failure. Cytotoxic (Puff Adder, Mozambique Spitting Cobra): severe pain, swelling, bruising. Haemotoxic (Boomslang): bleeding, renal failure.
Immobilise body part. Do NOT apply tourniquet, do NOT cut/incision, do NOT suction. Administer analgesia (Morphine).
Neuro/Cytotoxic: Polyvalent Antiserum (4-8 vials / 40-80ml) slow IV infusion. Haemotoxic: Monovalent Antivenom (4 vials / 40ml) slow IV.

warnings: Antivenom carries high risk of ANAPHYLAXIS. Always prepare resuscitation equipment, Adrenaline, and antihistamines beforehand.

management_steps.details: CT brain indicated if: GCS < 13 on initial, GCS < 15 at 2 hours, suspected skull fracture (raccoon eyes, Battle's sign, CSF leak, haemotympanum), post-traumatic seizure, >1 episode of vomiting, focal neuro deficit, or on anticoagulants.

Under 2 years: CT if GCS < 15, altered mental status, or palpable skull fracture. Observe vs CT if LOC > 5s, severe mechanism, or non-frontal hematoma. Over 2 years: CT if GCS < 15, altered mental status, or signs of basilar fracture.

Elevate head 30-45 degrees. Maintain MAP > 90 (unless ICH: MAP > 75-80). Keep normocarbia (PaCO2 35-40), normothermia (< 37.5), and euglycemia (5-10 mmol/L). If traumatic ICH: load with Phenytoin 20mg/kg IV (max rate 50mg/min) for seizure prophylaxis.

warnings: There is NO role for corticosteroids/steroids in traumatic head injury (increases mortality).

management_steps.details: Cool running water over burn for 20 mins if < 3 hours old. Clean wound, remove all blisters and debris. Estimate TBSA% using Lund and Browder chart.

Resuscitate with Ringers Lactate/Balsol if TBSA > 20% (adult) or > 15% (paeds): 2ml x TBSA% x Weight (kg). Infuse half in the first 8 hours, and the remainder over the next 16 hours. Target urine output: Adults 0.5-1 ml/kg/hr, Paeds 1-2 ml/kg/hr.
Indications: circumferential burns with vascular compromise (loss of distal pulse, severe pain, cyanosis). Incise deep along axial lines into subcutaneous tissue to breach constricting fascia.

Adult: Alvarado Score (RIF migratory pain [1], anorexia [1], nausea [1], RIF tenderness [2], rebound [1], fever [1], leukocytosis [2], left shift [1]). Paediatric (3-18 yrs): PAS score (cough/hopping tenderness [2], RLQ tenderness [2], anorexia [1], fever [1], nausea [1], WBC > 10 [1], neutrophilia [1], migratory pain [1]).
ABCD. Bolus fluids 20 ml/kg if hypovolaemic. If septic shock present: give Augmentin 30mg/kg IV, and arrange urgent surgical consult. Give Morphine 0.1mg/kg IV for pain.
RUQ / epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting, low-grade fever. Guarding, positive Murphy's sign (inspiratory pause on RUQ palpation).
Aesthetic criteria: gallstones/sludge AND 1+ of: GB wall thickening > 4mm, GB distension (diameter > 4cm, length > 10cm), pericholecystic fluid, ultrasonographic Murphy sign.
Augmentin 1.2g IV stat, antiemetics, and appropriate analgesia. Refer urgently to surgery.

Extremes of age (<20 or >50), malignancy history, constant non-mechanical pain (worse lying down/at night), any motor/sensory neuro deficit, bilateral symptoms, immunosuppression, IVDU, bowel/bladder dysfunction, fever.
Epidural Abscess: start broad antibiotics (Ceftriaxone, Cefazolin, or Vancomycin) and get urgent MRI. Suspected Spinal Metastases: give Dexamethasone 10mg IV stat and get urgent MRI.
Pain out of proportion to injury, pain on passive stretch, tense swollen compartment, decreased cap refill. Pulses are usually PRESENT (absent pulse is a late, catastrophic sign).
Normal: < 10 mmHg. Perform emergent Fasciotomy if: absolute compartment pressure > 30 mmHg OR perfusion pressure < 30 mmHg (DBP - compartment pressure).
Urgently consult ortho/general surgery. Remove all constrictive dressings/casts. Place limb AT THE LEVEL OF THE HEART (do not elevate). Avoid nerve blocks.
Crush Injury: physical injury from prolonged compression. Crush Syndrome: systemic manifestation of rhabdomyolysis leading to acute kidney injury (AKI) and hyperkalaemia.
Give isotonic crystalloids (Ringer's/Balsol) at 15-30 ml/kg/hr. Aim for high urine output of 200-300 ml/hr. If potassium is raised, avoid potassium-containing fluids.
Under expert consultation: give NaHCO3 8.5% (1ml/kg IV) to treat severe metabolic acidosis and correct hyperkalaemia. Consider Mannitol if urine output > 20ml/hr (contraindicated in anuria).

warnings: AVOID loop diuretics, synthetic colloids (Voluven/Gelofusin), and nephrotoxic drugs.
Indications for Dialysis: refractory acidosis, refractory hyperkalaemia, volume overload, or severe uraemia.

management_steps.details: Sudden onset severe, sharp, unilateral 'loin to groin' pain. Nausea/vomiting, haematuria, or LUTS. Ipsilateral renal angle tenderness.
Urine dipstix (haematuria), U&E, bedside ultrasound (check for hydronephrosis/hydroureter), or non-contrast CT KUB (gold standard).
First line: NSAIDs (Diclofenac 75mg IM or IV infusion over 30 mins) if no renal impairment. Opioids: Fentanyl 1 ug/kg IV or Morphine 0.1mg/kg. Antiemetic: Metoclopramide 10mg IV.

warnings: Urgent Urology Referral Indications: signs of infection/urosepsis, acute kidney injury (AKI), bilateral obstruction, obstruction in pregnancy, anuria, or obstruction of a solitary/transplant kidney.

management_steps.details: Clostridium tetani infection. Triad: rigidity (trismus/lockjaw, dysphagia), severe painful muscle spasms (laryngospasm, risus sardonicus, opisthotonos), and autonomic dysfunction (alternating tachycardia/bradycardia, hypertension/hypotension).

A (Intubate early to control airway spasm). B (Frequent suctioning for bronchial secretions). C (Autonomic stability: Magnesium Sulphate bolus and infusion). D (Benzodiazepines in large doses: up to 100mg/hr Diazepam).
Metronidazole IV (1st choice antibiotic). Anti-tetanus immunoglobulin (HTIG) 100-300 IU/kg IM. Clean and debride wounds thoroughly. Immunize (q10 yearly).

DKA: HGT > 11 (or known DM), younger, ketones positive, blood gas metabolic acidosis, anion gap > 16. HHS: HGT > 30, elderly, ketones absent/weak, minimal acidosis, serum osmolarity > 350, altered mental status.

ABCD. Large bore IV. Fluid resuscitation with Ringer's/Balsol: DKA (150-200ml/hr for 1st 4 hours), HHS (cautious, slower rate 100-200ml/hr). If shocked, give 20ml/kg bolus. When HGT < 15: change fluid to 5% Dextrose in Ringer's/Balsol.
Delay insulin if Potassium < 3.5! Add 20-40 mmol/L KCl to IV fluids to maintain K of 4-5. Add MgSO4 2g to maintenance fluids if low.
Give Actrapid 0.1 u/kg IV stat (max 10 u) followed by Actrapid infusion at 0.1 u/kg/hr. Perform hourly HGT monitoring.
Life-threatening emergency. Correct any HGT < 4 mmol/L immediately. If HGT unavailable, treat empirically.

If awake & swallows: give oral glucose/sugar. If unable: give 1-2 ml/kg of 50% Dextrose IV/IO. In children: dilute to max 25% dextrose (2-4 ml/kg of 25% dextrose). Start 5-10% dextrose maintenance fluid.
Add IV Hydrocortisone (steroids) if refractory. If sulfonylurea overdose: give Octreotide. Ensure early NGT feeds in intubated patients.

Correction needed if > 150. Estimate free water deficit: 0.6 * weight * ((Na/140) - 1). Infuse 5% Dextrose water or half-normal saline over 48 hours. Aim to correct Na by max 10-12 mmol/L in 24h (max 0.5 mmol/L/hr). Avoid correcting too fast (risk of cerebral edema). If central DI: DDAVP 1-2 ug IM/SC.

Severe CNS symptoms (seizures/coma, usually Na < 110): give 3% hypertonic saline 2ml/kg over 60 min to raise Na to 120. Once stable, limit increase to max 0.5 mmol/L/hr (max 12 mmol/L in 24h) to avoid pontine myelinolysis. Dehydrated: replace fluids (saline/Ringers). Oedematous: fluid restrict + Furosemide.

warnings: Hyponatraemia Warning: DO NOT correct chronic hyponatraemia too fast. Rapid correction carries high risk of irreversible osmotic demyelination syndrome / central pontine myelinolysis.

management_steps.details: Hyperthermia, tachycardia, altered mental GCS, heart failure. Diagnosis is CLINICAL (Burch-Wartofsky score >=45), do not wait for TSH! Give Propranolol 60-80mg PO q4h. Give PTU 600-1000mg PO loading dose, then 300mg q6h. Give Hydrocortisone 100mg IV q8h. Give Lugol's iodine 4-8 drops PO q6h (start 60 mins AFTER anti-thyroid drug to prevent thyroid hormone release).

Bradycardia, hypothermia, GCS stupor, hypotension, hyponatraemia, sepsis trigger. Urgent treatment: give Levothyroxine (Eltroxin) 300-500 mcg IV loading dose, then 50 mcg daily. Give Hydrocortisone 100mg IV q8h (covers concomitant adrenal insufficiency). Perform gentle active rewarming.

equipment: ET tubes (various sizes with cuff verified)
Oxygen (100% source, nasal cannula, FMO2, BVM)
Surgical airway kit (scalpel, size 6.0 ETT, permanent marker)

management_steps.details: Confirm all bedside equipment functions. Assess patient airway using LEMON criteria (Look externally, Evaluate 3-3-2, Mallampati, Obstruction, Neck mobility).
Pre-oxygenate with 100% O2 for 3-5 mins (nasal cannula + FMO2/BVM/NIV). Pre-load with 10-20ml/kg Balsol/Ringer's Lactate to prevent post-intubation hypotension.
Administer induction agent (Etomidate 0.3mg/kg or Ketamine 1-2mg/kg IV) followed by paralytic agent (Suxamethonium 1.5-2mg/kg or Rocuronium 1mg/kg IV).
Auscultate stomach (first) then bilateral chest. Confirm placement with end-tidal CO2 (ETCO2 waveform). Secure ETT at teeth (approx 21cm female, 23cm male).
Perform chest X-ray and ABG (after 30 mins). Start sedation/infusion (Morphine + Midazolam or Propofol). Connect to ventilator using Lung Protective settings.
L: Look externally (facial trauma, beard). E: Evaluate 3-3-2 rule. M: Mallampati. O: Obesity/Obstruction. N: Neck mobility.
Prepare for difficult intubation: 1 staff member assigned to intubate, 1 staff member scrubbed and ready at neck for surgical airway.

Use SCISSOR TECHNIQUE: (1) Identify cricothyroid membrane via 'laryngeal handshake'. (2) 4cm vertical midline skin incision. (3) Palpate membrane and make horizontal stab incision. (4) Turn scalpel 90 degrees or pass finger. (5) Insert bougie alongside. (6) Railroad size 6.0 ETT. (7) Confirm ETCO2.

Indications: cardiogenic pulmonary edema, acute COPD exacerbation, pre-oxygenation for RSI. Contraindications: cardiac/respiratory arrest, GCS depression, uncooperative, high aspiration risk, facial trauma.

Sit patient upright (>45 degrees). Select appropriate mask size. Strap firmly with complete seal. Start CPAP/NIV mode. Set PEEP of 4 cmH2O (increase in increments of 2 cmH2O). Set PSV initially on 0. Start with FiO2 1.0, titrate down rapidly.
Perfect for: neck of femur fractures, femoral shaft fractures, knee or patellar injuries, or anterior thigh lacerations.

Place patient supine. Clean and drape groin. Place linear transducer in inguinal crease to locate femoral nerve (lateral to pulsatile common femoral artery). Insert needle just below inguinal ligament, lateral to artery. Aspirate to avoid vessel. Infiltrate 20ml Marcaine (2-3mg/kg). Confirm local anaesthetic surrounds nerve.

warnings: Anaesthetises: anterior thigh, most of the femur, knee, and skin on the medial aspect of the lower leg.

management_steps.details: Plug into power (3 green LEDs). Plug O2 hose. Attach HME filter. Attach test lung to circuit. Switch ON (button on back-left). Machine defaults to VC-SIMV. Connect limbs to patient. Settings: FiO2 100% (titrate down), VT 6-8 ml/kg IBW, Ti 1.2-1.8s, RR 10-15, PEEP 6 mbar, dPSUPP 8-18 mbar. Swap expiratory valve after use.

Plug into power (lightning bolt charging icon). Connect O2. Attach specific circuit with flow sensor. Attach HME. Switch ON. Set patient sex and height to calculate IBW. Machine defaults to ASV mode. Set to 100% MinVol. Press START. Settings: O2 100%, MinVol 100%, flow trigger 4-5 L/min, P limit 30-35, PEEP 6.

protocols.item: Ultrasound Views: RUSH Protocol Scan Locations

management_steps.details: Evaluate 'the pump, the tank, and the pipes' in undifferentiated shock. Scan locations: (1) Heart: PSLA/PSSA, Apical 4-chamber. (2) IVC: subcostal. (3) Morison's: RUQ, LUQ, suprapubic (FAST exam). (4) Aorta: abdominal slide view. (5) Pulmonary: Right/Left anterior chest (check lung sliding).

Cardiogenic: poor contractility, plethoric IVC. Obstructive (Tamponade/PE): pericardial effusion with RA/RV collapse, dilated RV, plethoric IVC. Hypovolaemic: collapsing IVC, hyperdynamic heart, free fluid in Morison's pouch (ruptured ectopic/haemorrhage).

(1) Proximal Humerus: anterior shoulder, aim 45-degree angle toward opposite hip. (2) Proximal Tibia: 2cm medial or mid-point between medial/lateral along flat aspect of anterior tibia, 3cm below tibial tuberosity, aim 90 degrees. (3) Distal Tibia: 3cm proximal to medial malleolus, aim 90 degrees.

(1) Distal Femur: 1-2cm proximal to superior border of patella, 1cm medial to midline, aim 90 degrees. (2) Proximal Tibia: 1-2cm below patella, 1cm medial, aim 90 degrees. (3) Distal Tibia: 1-2cm proximal to medial malleolus, aim 90 degrees.

Clean site. Prepare driver and extension set. Push needle through skin until tip rests against bone (black line must be visible). Squeeze trigger with steady gentle pressure. Release trigger immediately upon feel of sudden 'give' or loss of resistance. Stabilize hub, remove stylet. Confirm placement (flush with saline).

Bradycardia: indicates CCB, BB, Digoxin, Clonidine, or lithium. Tachycardia: indicates anticholinergics, antihistamines, sympathomimetics (cocaine, amphetamines). AF: alcohol binge (holiday heart) or withdrawal. Ventricular Fibrillation: verapamil in AF+WPW.

PR Prolongation (>200ms): BB, CCB, Digoxin, TCA. QRS Prolongation (>100ms): Sodium channel blockade (TCA, carbamazepine, local anaesthetics, cocaine). QTc Prolongation: Potassium channel blockade (TCA, sotalol, antihistamines). J Wave: hypothermia. Scooped ST segment (Salvador Dali moustache): Digoxin.
Right Axis Deviation (terminal R wave > 3mm in aVR, or R/S ratio > 0.7 in aVR) indicates fast sodium channel blockade (highly predictive of TCA seizures/arrhythmias).
Place supine, elevate legs. Stop trigger.
0.5ml neat 1:1000 IM in anterolateral thigh. Repeat q3-5min if required.
20ml/kg Crystalloid bolus (Ringer's Lactate/Balsol). Airway management ready.
Hydrocortisone 200mg IV stat + Promethazine 12.5mg slow IV.

warnings: Biphasic reaction occurs in 5-20% of cases — monitor for 4-8 hours minimum
Avoid beta-blockers as they cause unopposed alpha-agonism during treatment

management_steps.action: Assess Airway & Prepare for difficult airway
management_steps.details: Stridor, drooling, dyspnoea are red flags. Double surgical setup ready.
If ACE-I induced (Bradykinin-mediated): Adrenaline, steroids, antihistamines are ineffective. Give Tranexamic Acid 1g IV over 10 min + FFP 2 units.
Verify Eye, Verbal, Motor responses (GCS 3-15)
Absolute indications: GCS <13 initially or <15 at 2 hours, open/depressed/base-of-skull fracture, post-traumatic seizure, focal neuro deficit, anticoagulants
Head up 30-45°, MAP >90 (unless ICH then >75-80), PCO2 34-40 (normocarbia), O2 sats >95% (normoxia), glucose 5-10 mmol/L, avoid neck pressure (C-spine collars)

warnings: Avoid steroids in traumatic intracranial hemorrhage — no therapeutic role

management_steps.details: Look for inhalation injury indicators: stridor, facial/neck burns, carbonaceous sputum

management_steps.action: Fluid Resuscitation via Modified Brooke Formula
management_steps.details: Formula: 2ml x %burn x Weight (kg) of Ringer's Lactate/Balsol. Give half over first 8 hours, half over next 16 hours. Indicated for adults >20% TBSA, children >15%.
Clean with sterile saline, debride blisters. Apply Jelonet and gauze. Face: Chloromex ointment (no dressing).
HGT >11, pH <7.3, HCO3 <18, Anion Gap >16, ketones positive. Hold insulin if K+ <3.3.
1L/hr for first 1-2 hours, then titrate to maintain urine output 1-2ml/kg/hr. Switch to Dextrose-containing fluids when HGT <15.
0.1 U/kg/hr Actrapid infusion. Maintain potassium at 4-5 mmol/L by adding KCl to fluid bags.

warnings: Delay insulin until potassium is >3.5 mmol/L to prevent precipitous drops
Avoid routine bicarbonate unless pH <6.8 and in severe shock

management_steps.details: Use LEMON criteria. Verify suction and alternative airways.
Align ear to sternal notch (sniffing position). Pre-oxygenate 100% for 3 min.
10-20ml/kg Ringer's Lactate/Balsol to offset induction-induced hypotension.
Induction (Ketamine 1-2mg/kg IV or Etomidate 0.3mg/kg IV) followed by paralytic (Suxamethonium 1.5mg/kg IV or Rocuronium 1mg/kg IV).

options.label: Localises pain
options.desc: Localises to painful stimulus (e.g. supraorbital pressure)

interpretation.label: Mild head injury
interpretation.action: Observe closely. Perform CT head if risk factors present.

interpretation.label: Moderate head injury
interpretation.action: Urgent CT Head and Neurosurgical consultation required.

interpretation.label: Severe head injury
interpretation.action: Intubate for airway protection. Urgent CT head and neurosurgical intervention.

interpretation.label: Low Risk
interpretation.action: C-spine imaging NOT indicated. Clinically clear.

canadian_cspine.name: Canadian C-Spine Rule
applicability: No known vertebral disease or previous C-spine surgery

components.name: Focal peripheral neurological deficit or paraesthesias

interpretation.label: Appendicitis Unlikely
interpretation.action: Consider other causes. Observe if pain persists.

interpretation.label: Appendicitis Possible
interpretation.action: Keep NPO, active observation, consider ultrasound.

interpretation.label: Appendicitis Probable/Highly Probable
interpretation.action: Urgent surgical consultation. Prepare for appendectomy.

components.name: Active cancer (treatment within 6 months or palliative)
Paralysis, paresis, or recent plaster immobilisation of lower extremity
Recently bedridden >=3 days or major surgery within 12 weeks
Localised tenderness along deep venous system
Calf swelling >3cm compared to asymptomatic leg
Pitting oedema confined to symptomatic leg
Alternative diagnosis as likely or more likely than DVT

interpretation.label: DVT Unlikely
interpretation.action: Perform D-dimer. If negative, exclude DVT. If positive, perform ultrasound.

interpretation.label: DVT Likely
interpretation.action: Perform formal compressive ultrasound of lower limb. Cautiously bridge with Clexane.

components.name: Clinical signs and symptoms of DVT
Alternative diagnosis is less likely than PE
Immobilisation >= 3 days or surgery in previous 4 weeks
Active cancer (treatment within 6 months or palliative)

interpretation.label: Low Risk
interpretation.action: Apply PERC only after confirming the patient is otherwise appropriate for the low-risk pathway.

interpretation.label: Moderate Risk
interpretation.action: Use the HJH pulmonary embolism algorithm, including age-adjusted D-dimer where applicable.

interpretation.label: High Risk
interpretation.action: Follow the HJH high-risk pathway: assess contraindications, anticoagulation, and CTPA eligibility.

perc.name: PERC Rule for PE Exclusion
applicability: Use only in the HJH low-risk pulmonary embolism pathway
All eight criteria must be explicitly confirmed

interpretation.label: High Risk (Mortality 15-40%)
interpretation.action: Urgent inpatient or ICU admission. Broad-spectrum IV antibiotics + steroid.

interpretation.label: Thyroid Storm Unlikely
interpretation.action: Perform thyroid function tests, manage supportively.

interpretation.label: Impending Thyroid Storm
interpretation.action: Highly suggestive of developing storm. Initiate therapy, consult endocrine.

interpretation.label: Thyroid Storm Highly Probable
interpretation.action: Clinical emergency. Admit ICU. Initiate PTU, Lugol's iodine, beta-blocker, steroids.
